title: Memdb serialization, deserialization, and store replacement

scope.rationale: These three source functions resolve a schema to a private memdb store, expose copied or borrowed database images, and replace a schema store with caller-provided bytes and ownership/resize/read-only flags. Native public APIs preserve main and attached private-schema copy/NOCOPY sizing, serialize ordinary databases from the live Pager page by page, and stage replacement buffers with source-shaped capacity, configured maximum, resize, ownership, and read-only flags before retiring the selected database; remaining source-side allocation-failure assurance remains open.
excluded_responsibilities: Memdb file methods and delegated VFS services assigned to memdb-file-storage-locking-and-mapping
Attached DDL, trigger/index maintenance, and foreign-key-enabled mutation semantics outside serialize/deserialize

dependencies.caller_closure: Public sqlite3_serialize/sqlite3_deserialize and backup APIs route through production Connection memory or Unix backend. Main and attached private-schema copy, NOCOPY borrow, replacement reopen, read-only mode, and FREEONCLOSE cleanup are reachable.

inputs: Connection, nullable/default schema, nullable size output, image pointer, database size, buffer capacity and ownership flags
outputs: Copied sqlite3_malloc image, borrowed private-memdb pointer, null with size, or exact result code
contracts.ownership: Copy serialization returns process-manager memory to caller. NOCOPY borrows store bytes. Deserialization transfers or borrows pData according to FREEONCLOSE and publishes no partial replacement on failure.
contracts.state_and_results: Size output begins at -1, successful schema resolution reports image size, NOCOPY succeeds only for private memdb, and deserialize sets size/capacity/max/flags before reopening schema.
contracts.locks_callbacks_io: Source holds connection then MemStore mutexes. Native serialized connection path uses MemoryVfs registry/store mutexes and may read Unix file bytes; no callbacks.
contracts.failure_and_continuation: Invalid connection/sizes return misuse, missing schema returns null/error, OOM returns null/NOMEM. Failure before replacement publication preserves the existing usable database, and every failure honors FREEONCLOSE exactly without double-free.

representation_differences: Private main-memory database lookup uses Connection.memory_backend instead of sqlite3_file_control plus memdb_io_methods identity.
NOCOPY now borrows the exact native main-store byte pointer and copied output uses the process memory manager.

Deserialize stages pData directly as native store bytes, retains the exact allocator-manager domain for realloc/free, preserves szDb/szBuf, applies max(szBuf, configured process memdb maximum), doubles reallocations up to that bound, and keeps post-replacement NOCOPY pointer identity.
Attached private stores are stable heap owners selected through the connection attachment catalog rather than source aDb/Btree file-control traversal.

oracle.protocol: Native SQL frontend and C ABI integration create memory and ordinary Unix database images, copy serialize with nullable size, NOCOPY borrow/rejection and exact size, clone the ordinary live Pager image through deserialize and execute its content, reject missing schema with size -1, enforce read-only opening, validate negative-capacity armor, preserve the old database on pre-publication allocation failure, publish malformed transferred storage before validation, preserve exact NOCOPY identity, return NOTADB on preparation and replacement, release FREEONCLOSE input at the correct owner, enforce the configured maximum, and inject realloc failure while checking exact pointer/content/size continuation. A maintained pinned C/Zig public-API differential compares deterministic private-store copy OOM with exact size output, copy size/header, main and attached-schema transfer/NOCOPY identity, schema-qualified attached query and bounded INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE continuation, READONLY reporting/write rejection, malformed deferred failure/replacement rejection, and close results.
oracle.normalization: Database image bytes, sizes, result codes and within-worker pointer identity are exact. Absolute C/Zig addresses are not compared.

assurance.oom: Pinned C/Zig evidence covers deterministic private-store copy OOM with exact size output; native fault injection also covers direct FREEONCLOSE close, borrowed storage, read-only storage, successful resize, configured maximum, pre-publication backend OOM, exact NOMEM, old-database continuation, input release, and allocator-manager realloc failure with unchanged pointer/content/size. The pinned differential also verifies attached-schema copy OOM with exact size and deserialize OOM with preserved old pointer, size, and close continuation.
assurance.io_crash_concurrency: Serialize, deserialize, and prepare hold the recursive connection mutex; ordinary databases copy the live Pager snapshot page by page, and pending deserialized images open under that mutex on first non-empty prepare. Exact concurrent misuse traces and cross-schema store lock ordering remain open.
assurance.malformed_input: Negative size/capacity, null data and unknown schema have native guards; the pinned differential verifies malformed publication, exact borrow identity, deferred NOTADB and replacement rejection. The full source API-armor matrix remains open.
assurance.continuation: Successful clone and subsequent SQL pass. Pre-publication allocation failure preserves queryable old content and releases FREEONCLOSE input; post-publication malformed storage remains borrowable, rejects use/replacement with NOTADB, and closes with exact ownership cleanup.
assurance.performance: NOCOPY is constant time. Copy serialization and ordinary Pager page iteration are linear in image size.

integration.native_call_path: C ABI sqlite3_serialize/sqlite3_deserialize -> Connection memory/Unix backend -> MemoryVfs/Pager reopen
integration.bounded_owner_retired: No separate test-only image owner; backup API uses these production exports.

independent_review.notes: Requires remaining source-side allocation-failure assurance and independent review.

known_blockers: Extend the pinned C/Zig differential with remaining source-side allocation-failure observations.

callers: Public sqlite3_serialize/sqlite3_deserialize exports and backup clone flow call this unit under the serialized connection path

Main and attached memory databases use private MemoryVfs images selected through the connection catalog, and schema-qualified scans plus bounded foreign-key-disabled DML execute the deserialized attached B-tree; named shared memdb denies NOCOPY; Unix serialization uses live Pager page count, page size, get, copy/zero-fill, and release operations
Deserialize closes/replaces the selected main or attached database, adopts caller storage, reopens Pager/Btree against the replacement, and later close frees storage only with FREEONCLOSE
callees: memdbFromDbSchema resolves through file control, verifies memdb methods, locks store, and returns only private zFName-null stores

Serialize initializes piSize to -1 after mutex entry, resolves schema, reports private-store size, borrows exact bytes for NOCOPY or sqlite3_malloc-copies them; ordinary Btree path obtains page count/page size and copies each page, zero-filling failed page gets

Deserialize rejects invalid handle/negative sizes, restricts temp schema, prepares ATTACH with reopenMemdb, resolves the new private store, transfers pData exactly once, publishes sz/szAlloc/szMax=max(buffer,global maximum)/flags, and frees untransferred FREEONCLOSE input on every failure

Native adoption records external pointer, logical size, capacity, resize/readonly/free flags; growth reallocates through process manager with source doubling/maximum and preserves pointer/content on failure
assertions_branches_cleanup: All 44 behavior IDs cover schema resolution, size initialization, private/shared/ordinary branches, NOCOPY, empty database materialization, allocation/page loop cleanup, deserialize armor/schema/reopen, transfer and failure FREEONCLOSE

Copy results are caller-owned sqlite3_malloc memory; NOCOPY is borrowed and only available for private stores; adopted bytes are borrowed or owned according to FREEONCLOSE and must not be double-freed

Native main/attached private-schema copy/NOCOPY/adoption paths, main readonly/resizable paths, ordinary Pager page-by-page copy, configured maximum, pre-publication OOM continuation, malformed post-publication ownership/error/close continuation, and exact realloc-failure pointer/content/size preservation are reachable and tested; attached copy and deserialize OOM match pinned source result, size, pointer, and continuation observations

Failure before transfer honors FREEONCLOSE; successful transfer leaves the replacement backend as owner before Pager validation, malformed storage remains NOCOPY-borrowable, first prepare and attempted replacement return NOTADB, and close releases the transferred image
upstream_tests: upstream memdb1.test covers main/attached serialization, direct/readonly/maxsize/empty/malformed deserialize, misuse, replacement restrictions, reopen and continuation; memdb.test/memdb2.test and corruption/fuzz suites exercise consumed images

Project SQL integration verifies nullable size, copy ownership, exact NOCOPY pointer/size, ordinary file Pager image size/header/NOCOPY rejection/deserialize query, missing schema size -1, negative-capacity armor, clone SQL, malformed publication success/exact pointer/deferred NOTADB/replacement rejection/ownership close, direct adopted-pointer identity, resizable growth, FREEONCLOSE, readonly reopen/write rejection and close; VFS injection verifies realloc OOM leaves the original manager allocation, content, and logical size unchanged
Backup integration routes through the same public exports, establishing a production caller; focused memdb tests cover byte-store size/limit/growth owners

The maintained pinned C/Zig public-API differential covers private-copy OOM/size reporting, main and attached-schema flags, ownership, malformed input, and continuation; remaining source-side OOM sites remain explicit blockers rather than claimed assurance
